rows.description: A senior you respect advises careful action, not a dramatic exit. Trust their experience on process, but stay clear that some lines cannot be crossed. Good mentors help you act right, not just act safe.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, coercion, fear, guilt, loyalty

rows.description: Asking for more money feels greedy and risky. Mature action: research market pay, state your value with examples, ask calmly, and be ready to hear no without taking it personally. Immature: silent resentment or ultimatums.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, envy, manipulation, pride, respect
related mind states: fear, calm, resentment

rows.description: A hiring manager who explains the pay band and the reasoning honestly is treating you as an adult. Respond with clear priorities, weigh the whole package, and do not confuse a fair no with disrespect.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, envy, fear, manipulation, pride

rows.description: Lines like we are a family or others would love this job try to make you feel ungrateful for asking. Recognise the pressure, stay polite, get details in writing, and remember that a fair employer welcomes a reasoned request.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, envy, fear, pride, respect

rows.description: You learn a peer earns more for the same role and feel your stomach drop. Use the information carefully: check facts, compare skills, and negotiate with evidence. Harmful: attacking the peer, or quitting on impulse.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, fear, manipulation, pride, respect

rows.description: Relatives push you to take the highest bid regardless of the work or city. Hear the worry behind it, but weigh growth, health and the culture too. Salary is one input, not the whole life.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, fear, manipulation, pride, respect

rows.description: You have a good offer and want to squeeze every rupee. Bargain firmly but honestly; bluffing about competing offers can wreck trust. A fair deal both sides can honour beats a win that sours the relationship.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, envy, fear, manipulation, respect

rows.description: You trust the company and want to sign fast. Wise: read the notice period, non-compete, IP, bond and penalty clauses, and ask questions. Trust is fine; ignoring paper is not. Good employers expect careful readers.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, deceit, dependence, guilt

rows.description: You rely on a lawyer, since you cannot parse clauses yourself. Ask them to explain risks in plain language, and note that the final decision is still yours. Blind reliance leaves you signing what you do not understand.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, deceit, guilt, trust

rows.description: Hidden fees, vague scope, or promises made verbally but missing on paper can signal deceit. Insist that agreed terms appear in writing, keep records, and walk away if they refuse. Pressure to sign today is a red flag.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, dependence, guilt, trust
